name: Stave
description: Low against high, ruled by the beat, in a room the stems tint. Two beaded traces scroll right-to-left across a ruled field, plotting the last eight seconds of the music as a time series. The lower trace is the low end (subBass+lowBass, each EMA-centred separately so a loud band cannot drag its partner's pivot); the upper is the top end (midHigh+highMid+high). They are near-independent on real music (r -0.27..+0.27 on 13 of 15 corpus tracks), so they read as two voices going their own way and crossing often rather than as two copies. Each trace is drawn as discrete beads on a faint thread, never a solid line — bead size rides the trace's own local slope, a derived geometric quantity rather than a fifth audio route, so the beads swell where the line is moving fast and shrink where it is flat. Per-trace gain is a precondition, not a knob: melodic energy runs 4.4-17.5x below rhythm across the corpus, so a shared gain would draw the top end as a flat line. Fixed gains with soft saturation tuned against p99, so a loud passage still LOOKS louder and only the extremes compress. The vertical rules are the actual beat, from the cached BeatGrid — median trace-to-beat offset measured at 0 ms on four captures, with the derived gridline rate matching grid_bpm exactly. Above roughly 150 bpm those rules stop reading as a pulse and start reading as graph paper, so their opacity fades with measured on-screen density — meter-free, needing no beatsPerBar, which the corpus says is unreliable within a single track. The horizontal rules are the stave itself and are static. The stems never touch a trace: they tint the whole field, slowly, via the drums+bass share of raw stem energy on an 8 s envelope, so a listener reads it as the room being warmer through a chorus and never as that mark is a snare. Behind it all: a horizon of haze, a five-octave cloud texture, and 4-point star sparkles scattered (not nodal) through the frame, all audio-independent so the field persists and drifts at silence while the traces flatline — a quiet passage flatlining IS the design. Milkdrop-inspired (D-113); diverges from its source on the primary feature stack (the source's rules are decoration, Stave's verticals are a real beat grid the source structurally cannot have), on compositional structure (4-8 undifferentiated traces there, 2 semantically assigned here), and on the dominant motion model (per-frame waveform geometry there, a scrolling 8 s history ring here).
author: Matt
